title: Minimax Regret of Smoothed Welfare Maximization for Threshold Policies
banked_reason: Its significance is limited by the deliberately narrow class, especially the fixed global welfare gap and crossing radii, and by the fact that the underlying smoothing exponent is already classical; the sharp minimax constant remains open.

proof_attempt_summary: The discovery proof completed a matched n^(-4/5) expected-regret result for a computable grid-smoothed threshold rule, a same-class converse for randomized learners, and an n^(-2/3) ordinary-EWM comparison. The math review passed, but the field-tier review found the fixed-gap/fixed-radii class and classical exponent insufficient for the field floor; no bounded same-scope revision was identified. A sharp minimax constant or a materially broader class remains a separate research program.
tldr: A known-half randomized trial identifies welfare for scalar threshold policies. Over one fixed nondegenerate class whose conditional treatment contrast has a unique \(C^2\) representative, a uniformly transversal crossing only within radius \(r_0=1/10\), and a separate global welfare gap \(\Delta_0=1/1000\), the deterministic-grid triweight welfare rule has uniform expected regret of order \(n^{-4/5}\). No randomized Markov-kernel threshold learner improves that order on the same trial class, while ordinary threshold EWM has worst-case expected regret of order \(n^{-2/3}\). Horowitz (1993) already establishes the analogous \(n^{-2/5}\) coefficient exponent for a kernel maximum-score rule in a binary-response model; the contribution here is therefore the uniform finite-sample causal-welfare theorem, the exact same-class trial converse, and the method comparison, not the kernel-rate exponent itself. The exact local asymptotic minimax constant remains an open question and is not part of the proved rate theorem.
gap: Crippa (2025) derives pointwise regret laws for EWM and SWM, notes that they do not imply convergence in mean, and asks whether the causal threshold rates are minimax. Horowitz (1993) establishes the \(n^{-h/(2h+1)}\) minimax coefficient exponent for a different binary-response experiment, but the accessible primary abstract does not supply a uniform finite-sample expected-welfare theorem, a computable global grid rule, or membership of its lower experiment in this fixed causal trial class.
fill: The project proves a logarithm-free finite-sample SWM bound by global-gap localization, local curvature of the unique smooth contrast representative, and one score moment; proves a full observed-data two-point converse against all Markov-kernel threshold learners; pins ordinary EWM's expected order on the identical class; and proves the exact boundary between the bounded binary lower subexperiment and the unrestricted bounded-outcome trial experiment. Fixed radii and numerical floors remain maintained threshold-policy restrictions needed for uniformity and same-class witness slack, not conclusions or borrowed assumptions.
